name: load_executable_hunks
description: Program entry that gets the current task and allocates memory through the exec library, then walks a chain of hunk records, comparing their type codes and linking the allocated blocks together. It also frees memory through exec, so it reads as executable loading or relocation code.

name: return_without_work
description: A bare return with no observable work, called from elsewhere in the program. It has no side effects.

name: burn_delay_cycles
description: Counts a register down through zero in a tight loop, consuming time without touching memory or hardware. Three other routines call it, so it acts as a fixed busy-wait delay.

name: unpack_run_length_stream
description: Decodes a packed byte stream into memory, writing backwards from a destination pointer. A zero flag starts a run of one repeated byte, other values copy a counted sequence, and the loop stops when the source reaches its end. Its called routines also touch the background colour register, so it is probably a picture or palette unpacker.

name: decrement_byte_with_wrap
description: Decrements a byte in register D7 once for each count passed in D0, substituting a space character when the byte wraps to zero. It makes no memory accesses or calls, so its only effect is on that register.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Contains bad instruction data that the disassembler read as code, so decompilation stops after the first instruction. There is no real behaviour to describe here.

name: copy_longwords_then_call
description: If a destination pointer is supplied, copies sixteen 32-bit longwords from a fixed table in the program into it. It then calls through a function pointer held in a register, so it relays control to a library or handler routine.

name: build_echo_output_buffer
description: Entry point of the echo command. It loops over a linked list to find the largest length value, sets up a buffer on the stack, and calls library routines through a function vector to allocate memory and fill in the output records.

name: copy_longwords_then_call
description: If a destination pointer is supplied, copies sixteen 32-bit longwords from a fixed table in the program into it. It then calls through a function pointer held in a register, so it relays control to a library or handler routine.

name: return_minus_one
description: Library stub in the math library that returns the value minus one, with every bit set, to the caller. It has no other effect.

name: initialise_mathieee_resource
description: Allocates a structure through the exec library and fills in its handler pointers, a flag read from the library base, and a data pointer. If that flag is clear, it looks up the MathIEEE resource by name and copies its data pointer, then makes a closing library call to finish setup.

name: allocate_and_fill_request
description: Allocates a structure through an exec library call and stores two handler pointers, a flag, a supplied value, the library base and a supplied pointer in its fields. If a second structure is given, it notifies that structure's handler before a closing library call.

name: raise_math_error_trap
description: Sets a status word in a supplied structure to a fixed value, then raises a divide-by-zero or trap-on-overflow error depending on the operation code. It is the error handler the math library uses for those codes.

name: raise_error_in_two_bands
description: Returns early for operands outside two fixed ranges, and otherwise sets a status word and raises the same divide-by-zero or trap-on-overflow error as its neighbours. Only operands inside the two bands reach the error code.

name: raise_error_outside_middle_band
description: Returns early for operands inside a middle range, and otherwise sets a status word and raises the same divide-by-zero or trap-on-overflow error.

name: raise_error_in_band
description: Returns early for operands outside one fixed range, and otherwise sets a status word and raises the same divide-by-zero or trap-on-overflow error.

name: raise_error_below_limit
description: Returns early for operands above a fixed upper limit, and otherwise sets a status word and raises the same divide-by-zero or trap-on-overflow error.

name: poll_device_then_return
description: Loops reading a 16-bit device word until it is no longer a start marker, then waits for the device to report a non-negative status. It writes control words to a nearby register and returns the stored long as a 64-bit value.

name: await_device_then_store
description: Waits on a device status word, stores a value returned by a helper into an output slot, and writes a control word to a nearby register. It then waits for the device to report a non-negative status and returns the stored value as a 64-bit result.

name: wait_for_device_ready
description: Repeats a helper call while a start marker is present, writing a control word to a nearby register each time, then waits for the device status to become non-negative. It returns the value already stored in the output slot as a 64-bit result.

name: poll_device_status_word
description: Clears a status word and returns its high byte if that byte is set. Otherwise it polls a device word, writes a control word to it, and returns zero after recording a fixed error code if the device reports a failure.

name: wait_device_control_reply
description: Waits until a device word is non-negative, writes a control word to it, and polls until the device replies. On an error reply it stores the fixed error code 144 in an output slot and returns zero.

name: report_fixed_error_code
description: Repeatedly calls a helper while the device word shows a start marker, writing a control word each time. It then stores the fixed error code 144 in an output slot, waits for the device to be ready, and returns zero.

name: classify_double_operands
description: Splits two double-precision operands into sign and exponent, handles the infinity and zero cases, and calls helper routines for ordinary values. It returns a 64-bit result, so it is the front end of the floating point arithmetic.

name: return_special_double_case
description: Handles special operands by returning a not-a-number pattern when both operands match a special value. Otherwise it returns a sign-adjusted zero or special result.

name: return_nan_constant
description: Returns a fixed 64-bit not-a-number pattern and nothing else. It is the library's answer for invalid floating point operations.

name: return_signed_zero_case
description: When both low operand words are zero, returns a 64-bit value built from the operand in A0 and the stored sign word. Otherwise it returns the sign word shifted into the top bits of the result.

name: return_exponent_xor_word
description: Returns a 64-bit value whose top word is a stored word exclusive-ored with the exponent mask, with all other bits zero. It is the tail of a special-value path.

name: resolve_double_exponent_case
description: Compares a 16-bit exponent value with an operand and, when the masked bits overlap, calls helper routines to build the double result. Otherwise it returns a sign-adjusted fraction or a special pattern.

name: return_signed_zero_word
description: Returns the stored sign word in the top 16 bits of a 64-bit result, with zeros elsewhere. It is the zero result for a special operand.

name: resolve_double_zero_case
description: Checks whether the masked bits of the first operand are zero. If they are, it returns a not-a-number pattern or a signed zero, and otherwise calls helper routines to finish the double operation.

name: return_signed_zero_word
description: Returns the stored sign word in the top 16 bits of a 64-bit result, with zeros elsewhere. It is the zero result for a special operand.

name: finish_double_masked_result
description: Calls a helper for the 64-bit value, then tests one masked bit of the operand. When that bit is clear it builds the result from the stored operand and sign word, and otherwise calls another helper.

name: combine_double_fraction_parts
description: Combines the fraction parts of two operands, applying a helper call and a sign word correction before returning a 64-bit result. It is a middle stage of the double arithmetic.

name: divide_double_mantissas
description: Subtracts exponent fields using a fixed bias, then divides the shifted mantissa parts with a 32-bit division and keeps the remainder. It is the division step of the double-precision library.

name: divide_double_alt_bias
description: Divides shifted mantissa parts with a 32-bit division after subtracting exponents with a different fixed bias. It is a variant of the division step for the other exponent range.

name: divide_double_fraction_bits
description: Shifts a two-word fraction and divides it with a 32-bit division to produce quotient bits, calling a helper along the way. It is the bit-generation loop of the division.

name: multiply_double_mantissas
description: Multiplies two 64-bit mantissas by splitting them into 16-bit halves and summing the partial products with carries. It leaves the 64-bit product in the result registers after a helper call.

name: subtract_partial_products_fraction
description: Forms a 64-bit difference from 16-bit partial products, decrementing the high word when a borrow occurs, and then calls a helper. It is a correction step in the mantissa arithmetic.

name: normalise_double_mantissa
description: Shifts a mantissa left by sixteen bits while its top bit is clear, adjusting the exponent to match. It normalises the result so the leading bit sits in the expected position.

name: shift_mantissa_right_exponent
description: Shifts a 64-bit mantissa right by an amount taken from an exponent difference, in sixteen-bit steps for large amounts. If the shift is too large it returns a signed zero, and otherwise it returns the shifted value.

name: shift_mantissa_right_loop
description: Repeatedly shifts a 64-bit mantissa right in sixteen-bit steps until the remaining count is under sixteen, then finishes the shift and returns the result. It is the inner loop of the mantissa shifter.

name: pack_double_with_exponent
description: Adds an exponent field to a double result and returns the packed value when it stays in range. If the exponent falls below range it shifts the mantissa right instead, and if it overflows it returns the largest finite value.

name: normalise_and_pack_double
description: Checks the implicit bit of a mantissa and, when it is clear, shifts it left while decrementing the exponent. It then packs the sign and exponent back into a 64-bit double, shifting right first if the exponent is too small.

name: return_largest_finite_double
description: Returns the largest finite double value with the sign applied and all mantissa bits set. It is the overflow result of the arithmetic.

name: normalise_mantissa_by_table
description: Finds the shift needed to bring the leading one of a 64-bit value into position, using a byte lookup table and two shifts. It then shifts the mantissa and returns the normalised pair.

name: normalise_pair_by_table
description: Uses a byte lookup table to find a normalising shift for a word pair, then shifts the second word and mixes its bits with the first. It returns the normalised 64-bit value.

name: shift_double_right_count
description: Shifts a 64-bit value right by a count derived from a 16-bit exponent value, folding bits into the low part and applying the stored sign to the top word. It is a denormalising helper.

name: return_signed_zero_word
description: Returns the stored sign word in the top 16 bits of a 64-bit result, with zeros elsewhere. It is the zero result for a special operand.

name: return_signed_zero_word
description: Returns the stored sign word in the top 16 bits of a 64-bit result, with zeros elsewhere. It is the zero result for a special operand.

name: return_largest_finite_double
description: Returns the largest finite double value with the sign applied and all mantissa bits set. It is the overflow result of the arithmetic.

name: return_exponent_xor_word
description: Returns a 64-bit value whose top word is a stored word exclusive-ored with the exponent mask, with all other bits zero. It is the tail of a special-value path.

name: return_nan_constant
description: Returns a fixed 64-bit not-a-number pattern and nothing else. It is the library's answer for invalid floating point operations.

name: make_quiet_nan_value
description: Sets a flag bit in a 32-bit value to mark it as a quiet not-a-number, then shifts the high word into the top bits. It converts a value into the library's quiet form.

name: stub_unimplemented_instruction
description: Library entry point that contains only an unimplemented instruction, so decompilation stops immediately. It has no real behaviour to describe.

name: open_basic_math_library
description: Opens the basic math library by name through an exec call. If that succeeds, it looks up the MathIEEE resource when the flag bit is clear, allocates a structure, and stores handler pointers and the library base in it, so the transcendental library can depend on it.

name: initialise_transcendental_handler
description: Looks up the MathIEEE resource by name when the flag bit is clear, allocates a structure, and stores handler pointers, a data pointer and the library base in it. It is the same setup as the basic library's open code, for the transcendental library.

name: allocate_transcendental_request
description: Allocates a structure through an exec library call, stores handler pointers, a flag, a supplied value, the library base and a supplied pointer, then notifies a second structure when given. It finishes with a library call.

name: raise_math_error_trap
description: Raises a divide-by-zero for operation code 50 and a trap-on-overflow for operation code 53, without setting a status word. It is the error trap used by the transcendental library.

name: raise_error_in_two_bands
description: Returns early for operands outside two fixed ranges, and otherwise raises the divide-by-zero or trap-on-overflow error. Only operands inside the two bands reach the error code.

name: raise_error_outside_middle_band
description: Returns early for operands inside a middle range, and otherwise raises the divide-by-zero or trap-on-overflow error for the operation code. It is the same guard as its neighbours in the transcendental library.

name: raise_error_in_band
description: Returns early for operands outside one fixed range, and otherwise raises the divide-by-zero or trap-on-overflow error for the operation code.

name: raise_error_below_limit
description: Returns early for operands above a fixed upper limit, and otherwise raises the divide-by-zero or trap-on-overflow error for the operation code.

name: return_without_work
description: A bare return with no observable work, so calling it has no side effects.

name: write_double_to_device
description: Packs the two 32-bit halves of a double into a device output slot through a control word, then polls the device until it replies. It returns the packed value as a 64-bit result.

name: await_device_then_store
description: Waits on a device status word, stores a value returned by a helper into an output slot, and writes a control word to a nearby register. It then waits for the device to report a non-negative status and returns the stored value as a 64-bit result.

name: wait_for_device_ready
description: Repeats a helper call while a start marker is present, writing a control word to a nearby register each time, then waits for the device status to become non-negative. It returns the value already stored in the output slot as a 64-bit result.

name: send_double_arguments_to_device
description: Sends two 32-bit arguments to the device, writing control words before and after, and polls until the device is ready. It returns the result word pair as a 64-bit value.

name: await_device_store_pair
description: Waits for the device, stores two supplied 32-bit values into the output slot, and writes a control word before waiting again. It returns the stored pair as a 64-bit result.

name: store_stack_args_to_device
description: Waits for the device, stores two stack arguments into the output slot, then issues a sequence of control words to the device. It returns the stored value as a 64-bit result.

name: await_device_then_return
description: Repeatedly calls a helper while the device word shows a start marker, writing a control word each time. It then waits until the device is ready and returns the stored value as a 64-bit result.

name: return_zero_value
description: Returns zero in the result register and does nothing else, so a caller gets a zero result with no side effects.

name: compute_exponential_value
description: Computes an exponential by multiplying its argument by a constant close to the base-two logarithm of e, using helper calls for the arithmetic. It returns one when the argument is zero and otherwise a 64-bit double.

name: guard_exponential_argument_range
description: Compares the argument with large positive and negative limits, returning early or calling helpers depending on whether it falls inside the representable range. It is the range guard for the exponential computation.

name: handle_exponential_upper_limit
description: Compares the argument with an upper limit, and if it lies inside the limit calls helpers to compute the reduced argument and its scaled result. It is the upper-bound branch of the exponential guard.

name: compute_exp_by_reduction
description: Runs the main exponential computation: it reduces the argument by a multiple of the logarithm constant, evaluates a series with helper calls, and scales the result by a power of two. It is the largest routine in the exponential code and calls nine helpers.

name: scale_double_by_power_two
description: Adds an integer exponent to the exponent field of a double, returning zero for results below range, the adjusted value in range, and a saturated maximum when it overflows. It is the power-of-two scaling step.

name: adjust_double_exponent_field
description: Adds an offset to the exponent field of a double after checking the offset is within range, and saturates to a large constant otherwise. It returns the adjusted double.

name: adjust_exponent_field_unchecked
description: Adds an offset to the exponent field of a double without a range check, then returns the adjusted value. It is the simple form of the exponent adjustment.

name: evaluate_polynomial_reduction
description: Reduces a value around the square root of one half and evaluates a series of double-precision constants, using helper calls for each step. It returns the result as a 64-bit double, which suggests a logarithm-type function.

name: compute_logarithm_by_reduction
description: Splits a double into an exponent and a mantissa scaled near one, compares the mantissa with the square root of one half, and calls helpers for a polynomial-style series. It looks like the main logarithm routine and returns a 64-bit double.

name: compute_power_value
description: Computes one value raised to a double exponent: it returns one when the exponent is zero, and otherwise calls helpers for the logarithm and exponential steps. It takes a function pointer too, so the inner step can be supplied by the caller.

name: combine_power_partial_results
description: Combines the integer and fractional parts of a power-style computation by calling helpers, with a branch for a zero operand. It works on values held in the stack frame and supports the power routine.

name: return_one_constant
description: Stores zero in a scratch slot and returns the double value one. It is the result for a power or exponential case where the answer is one.

name: handle_power_special_cases
description: Checks the operands for zero, sign and very large magnitude, returning a not-a-number pattern or continuing to the computation when the operands are in range. It is the special-case front end of the power routine.

name: compute_small_integer_power
description: Raises a value to an integer power. A negative exponent is negated first, small exponents are handled by repeated multiplication, and larger ones call a helper.

name: repeat_power_multiplication
description: Repeats a helper multiplication for the count in a register, storing each intermediate double in the frame and keeping the last one. It is the loop used for larger integer powers.

name: combine_parity_power_steps
description: Combines operands through four helper calls, alternating between two intermediate doubles depending on the parity of an integer count. It is a squaring-style step of the power routine.

name: dispatch_guarded_double_op
description: If the second operand is zero or its sign is wrong, returns zero. Otherwise it calls the operation supplied in a function pointer with four 32-bit operands and returns the 64-bit result.

name: dispatch_double_operation
description: Calls the operation supplied in a function pointer with two 64-bit operands, storing and returning the 64-bit result. It is the unguarded form of the dispatch.

name: return_zero_value
description: Returns zero in the result register and does nothing else, so a caller gets a zero result with no side effects.

name: chain_three_double_steps
description: Passes a 64-bit value through three helper calls in sequence and returns the final result. It is a composition wrapper for the library's double operations.

name: rebias_double_exponent_field
description: Subtracts the bias from the exponent field of a double, zeroing the whole value when the result is below range and otherwise writing the rebiased field back. It works in place on the four words of the value.

name: set_double_exponent_field
description: Writes a biased exponent value into the exponent field of a double in place, keeping the sign and mantissa bits. It is the store-only form of the exponent adjustment.

name: dispatch_indexed_routine
description: Calls a routine found by adding a stored base value to a register offset, so it dispatches to one of several entries in a jump table. It is a table-driven call helper.

name: jump_to_vector_minus78
description: Calls the library routine at a fixed offset of minus 78 from the stored base, passing control through with no other work. It is one entry of the library's vector table.

name: jump_to_vector_minus66
description: Calls the library routine at a fixed offset of minus 66 from the stored base, passing control through with no other work. It is one entry of the library's vector table.

name: jump_to_vector_minus72
description: Calls the library routine at a fixed offset of minus 72 from the stored base, passing control through with no other work. It is one entry of the library's vector table.

name: jump_to_vector_minus84
description: Calls the library routine at a fixed offset of minus 84 from the stored base, passing control through with no other work. It is one entry of the library's vector table.

name: jump_to_vector_minus42
description: Calls the library routine at a fixed offset of minus 42 from the stored base, passing control through with no other work. It is one entry of the library's vector table.

name: dispatch_indexed_routine
description: Calls a routine found by adding a stored base value to a register offset, dispatching through a jump table. It is the table-driven dispatch helper.

name: jump_to_vector_minus30
description: Calls the library routine at a fixed offset of minus 30 from the stored base, passing control through with no other work. It is one entry of the library's vector table.

name: jump_to_vector_minus36
description: Calls the library routine at a fixed offset of minus 36 from the stored base, passing control through with no other work. It is one entry of the library's vector table.

name: jump_to_basic_library_minus54
description: Calls a routine in the basic math library through the vector at minus 54 from the stored base, with no other work. It forwards the call to that library.

name: jump_to_basic_library_minus90
description: Calls a routine in the basic math library through the vector at minus 90 from the stored base, with no other work. It forwards the call to that library.

name: install_runtime_code_patches
description: Sets a flag bit, calls a routine, then writes jump and return instruction words into several fixed addresses in the program's code so calls go to local routines. It then calls a stored pointer, so it installs code patches before the program continues.

name: wait_flag_then_enable_dma
description: Waits for a status flag bit to become set and then clear, then writes a DMA control word that enables several channels. It is a hardware sequence rather than program logic.

name: wait_for_counter_threshold
description: Repeatedly reads a value from a helper until it is at least 150, then returns. It is a timing wait that paces the code on a counter.

name: fade_palette_entries_down
description: Waits until a helper value reaches 100, then repeatedly steps each colour entry's three 4-bit components down by one, repeating until all entries reach zero. It reads like a palette fade-out.

name: patch_game_code_returns
description: Writes return instructions, jump instructions and branch words into many fixed addresses of the program's code, disabling some routines and redirecting others. It is a second patch installer, run alongside the first.

name: toggle_two_low_bits
description: Flips the low two bits of the value in a register with exclusive-or, leaving the other bits unchanged. It is a simple state toggle.

name: start_blit_and_wait
description: Starts a blitter operation by writing a size word, then polls the blitter busy flag until the blitter finishes. It is a short synchronous blit call.

name: apply_conditional_code_patches
description: Calls a routine through a pointer in a stored structure, then compares a passed-in value with fixed magic values and writes jump instructions into code locations when they match. It also writes a branch when a computed product matches a fixed value.

name: copy_byte_into_word_field
description: Copies a byte from one structure into a 16-bit field of another, zero-extending it. It is a simple field-transfer step.

name: reset_global_variable
description: Sets a global variable to zero, repeating the store three times, and does nothing else. It resets state the caller depends on.

name: replicate_global_byte_pattern
description: Returns the global byte repeated across the low three bytes of a 32-bit result. It builds a fill pattern from one stored byte.

name: trap_and_check_count
description: Issues a trap, subtracts three from a stored count, then checks it and a table value before calling two fixed routines. Most branches end in bad instruction data, so only this partial logic can be read.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Consists of conditional bad instruction data that the disassembler could not read as real code, so it has no behaviour to describe.

name: stub_no_instructions
description: The address decodes to no instructions, so there is no routine here. It has no behaviour to describe.

name: setup_disk_loader_hardware
description: Clears a block of low memory, sets the disk controller to MFM mode with the standard sync word, waits on the raster position, and builds and installs a copper list. It then enables DMA and appears to start disk reads, so it is the disk loader's hardware setup.

name: update_timed_entry_table
description: Walks a table of records, counting each record's first word down toward zero. For records whose type code matches one of two values it performs a per-type action through a helper, and it stops at a sentinel value.

name: dispatch_matching_table_entries
description: Loops over up to thirty-five keys, scans a table of seven-word records for each key, and calls a helper on every match. It stops when the key counter reaches its limit.

name: program_blitter_from_table
description: Advances a cyclic table pointer, updates two running values, and programs the blitter modulo registers from the current entry unless it is the end marker. It is the table-driven blitter setup.

name: setup_blit_area_and_start
description: Sets the blitter's first and last word masks, computes an area size from two inputs, writes modulo and offset registers, and calls helpers to start the blit. It is a general blit setup routine called from several places.

name: wait_for_blitter_idle
description: Polls the blitter busy flag until it clears, then returns. It is used to wait for a blit to finish before the blitter is reprogrammed.

name: setup_blit_area_from_pointer
description: Like its neighbour, sets the blitter masks and modulo registers from a computed area size, but takes a source pointer from an argument and calls helpers to start the blit.

name: step_two_counters_toward_limit
description: Moves two counters toward their limits: one counts down to zero while the other increases, and the second steps by two until it reaches a fixed value. It calls helpers to apply the change, making it a small timing update.

name: clip_rectangle_to_bounds
description: Clips a rectangle's horizontal and vertical positions against fixed screen bounds, moving values in sixteen-unit steps. It is the clipping step before an object is drawn.

name: clear_work_buffer
description: Calls a helper for the buffer address, then writes zero to eleven thousand consecutive longwords. It clears a large work area such as a screen bitmap.

name: wait_for_frame_counter
description: Waits until a counter reaches four, then resets it to zero. The counter is incremented by an interrupt handler, so this synchronises the code with the interrupt tick.

name: swap_bitplane_pointers
description: Toggles a flag between two states and writes four bitplane addresses into a pointer table, stepping each by a fixed block size. It switches between two frame buffers.

name: return_without_work
description: Tests a flag and returns in both cases, so it has no observable effect.

name: handle_tick_interrupt
description: Interrupt handler that writes an interrupt-request acknowledge value to the hardware and increments the shared tick counter. The wait routine counts these ticks.

name: decode_signed_sample_stream
description: Reads words from a stream through a helper and converts their low bits into signed values, storing them in three output locations until the loop counter reaches zero. It decodes a packed stream into signed values.

name: advance_random_seed
description: Updates a stored 32-bit value by adding a constant to its low word, shifting and exclusive-oring it, then swapping its halves. It is a pseudo-random number step.

name: plot_pixel_four_bitplanes
description: Checks that a point lies inside a 320 by 200 area, then sets the matching bit in each of four bitplanes whose colour index bits are set. Rows are 44 bytes apart and the planes are a fixed distance apart.

name: cycle_table_bytes
description: Walks one hundred words in a table after calling a helper, adding eight to each and keeping only its low byte. It steps the values in the table.

name: set_bounds_limits_return_byte
description: Stores two fixed limits of 63 and two of 400 into a structure, then returns the input byte with its low bits forced on. It configures a bounds structure.

name: set_bounds_limits
description: Stores fixed limits of 63 and 400 into four fields of a structure. It is the void form of the limits setup.

name: set_audio_channel_pair
description: Stores a start address and a length into audio channels 0 and 2, then writes a DMA control word that enables them. It starts a pair of audio samples.

name: set_audio_channel_pair
description: Stores a start address and a length into audio channels 0 and 2, then writes a DMA control word that enables them. It starts a pair of audio samples.

name: set_audio_channel_pair
description: Stores a different start address and length into audio channels 0 and 2, then writes a DMA control word that enables them. It starts a pair of audio samples.

name: wait_audio_sample_end
description: Acknowledges the audio interrupt bits, waits until the first audio channel signals an interrupt, then acknowledges again and turns off DMA for two channels. It stops a sound once its sample has finished.

name: wait_for_status_bits
description: Spins until at least one of two status bits in a global variable is clear, then returns those two bits inverted. The global mirrors the joystick and disk status port, so this waits on those inputs.

name: handle_interrupt_countdown
description: Interrupt handler that acknowledges the interrupt request, increments the shared tick counter and counts a second counter down. When that counter reaches zero it is reset to six; otherwise a fixed routine is called. Both paths then write the flag value 255 to a global variable.

name: reset_interrupt_countdown
description: Resets the interrupt countdown to six and writes the flag value 255 to a global variable. It is the reset path of the countdown interrupt.

name: execute_infinite_loop
description: Spins forever with no work inside the loop, so control never returns to the caller.

name: poll_until_zero
description: Calls a routine repeatedly until its short result is zero, then returns. It waits for a helper to report completion.

name: expand_bitmask_stream
description: Expands a stream of 16-bit mask words into output words: each set mask bit copies the next source word, and each clear bit writes zero. It runs over 1250 mask words.

name: clear_port_control_bit
description: Clears one control bit in a global variable, then calls four helper routines that touch the CIA port. It is a short sequencing step in hardware access.

name: start_disk_dma_read
description: Points the disk DMA at a buffer, enables disk DMA and starts a read by writing the disk length register. It then polls the disk block-done interrupt bit with a limit of 200000 iterations and retries if it never appears.

name: search_disk_sync_words
description: Scans a buffer of longwords for a disk sync pattern, counts the data words that follow, and stores a result flag depending on whether the count is below a threshold. It is the sector-search step of the disk reader.

name: verify_block_checksums
description: Calls a helper and sums 3100 words from a source pointer, comparing the sum with the word that follows the block. It advances by the block size for the requested number of blocks, so it verifies block checksums.

name: decode_mfm_words_to_buffer
description: Fills 3100 words of a destination buffer from a source table by combining alternate bits with a mask and exclusive-oring the result with a supplied value. It is an MFM-style decode step on the track data.

name: read_track_blocks_until_marker
description: Repeats a disk read into successive buffers, starting each DMA transfer with the same length word, until the buffer's first longword equals a fixed marker value. It then stops disk DMA.

name: acknowledge_disk_block_done
description: Waits for the disk block-done interrupt bit to be set, then writes the interrupt acknowledge for that bit.

name: delay_then_wait_flag
description: Runs a fixed countdown of three thousand steps, then spins until bit five of a global variable is clear. It delays briefly and then waits for a status flag.

name: seek_drive_head_to_track
description: Moves a stored position value toward a target one step at a time, setting direction bits in a global port value and calling a helper for each step. It is the seek routine for the disk head.

name: wait_drive_status_then_clear
description: Repeats a helper call while bit four of a global variable remains set, then clears the global variable. It waits for a drive status bit to drop before finishing.

name: wait_for_flag_bit_set
description: Spins until bit four of a global variable is set, then returns. The global mirrors a CIA interrupt status, so this waits for that event.

name: clear_port_bits_with_delay
description: Clears bit seven of a global variable, clears bit three on each step of a fixed countdown of 100, then calls a helper. It is a timed bit-clearing step on a port mirror.

name: set_port_bit_with_delay
description: Sets bit seven of a global variable, runs a fixed countdown of 100 steps that clears bit three, then sets bit three. It is a timed bit-setting step on a port mirror.

name: fade_palette_toward_target
description: Repeatedly steps each colour word in a 32-entry table toward a target table, adding to each 4-bit component until the entries match, and calls helpers between passes. It behaves like a palette fade-in.

name: fade_palette_entries_down
description: Repeatedly steps each colour entry's three 4-bit components down by one until all entries reach zero, calling helpers between passes. It reads like a palette fade-out.

name: report_undecoded_large_routine
description: This 461-instruction routine could not be decoded, so its pseudo-code is unavailable and its behaviour cannot be stated. The available facts show it is called from two places and that its address is used by absolute compare and move instructions elsewhere.

name: report_undecoded_jump_caller
description: This 167-instruction routine could not be decoded, so its pseudo-code is unavailable and its behaviour cannot be stated. The available facts show it calls an empty stub, a jump-table entry and twenty other routines, and touches the fire-button and disk status port.

name: update_timed_entry_table
description: Walks a table of records, counting each record's first word down toward zero. For records whose type code matches one of two values it performs a per-type action through a helper, and it stops at a sentinel value.

name: dispatch_matching_table_entries
description: Loops over up to thirty-five keys, scans a table of seven-word records for each key, and calls a helper on every match. It stops when the key counter reaches its limit.

name: program_blitter_from_table
description: Advances a cyclic table pointer, updates two running values, and programs the blitter modulo registers from the current entry unless it is the end marker. It is the table-driven blitter setup.

name: setup_blit_area_and_start
description: Sets the blitter's first and last word masks, computes an area size from two inputs, writes modulo and offset registers, and calls helpers to start the blit. It is a general blit setup routine called from several places.

name: wait_for_blitter_idle
description: Polls the blitter busy flag until it clears, then returns. It is used to wait for a blit to finish before the blitter is reprogrammed.

name: setup_blit_area_from_pointer
description: Like its neighbour, sets the blitter masks and modulo registers from a computed area size, but takes a source pointer from an argument and calls helpers to start the blit.

name: step_two_counters_toward_limit
description: Moves two counters toward their limits: one counts down to zero while the other increases, and the second steps by two until it reaches a fixed value. It calls helpers to apply the change, making it a small timing update.

name: clip_rectangle_to_bounds
description: Clips a rectangle's horizontal and vertical positions against fixed screen bounds, moving values in sixteen-unit steps. It is the clipping step before an object is drawn.

name: clear_work_buffer
description: Calls a helper for the buffer address, then writes zero to eleven thousand consecutive longwords. It clears a large work area such as a screen bitmap.

name: wait_for_frame_counter
description: Waits until a counter reaches four, then resets it to zero. The counter is incremented by an interrupt handler, so this synchronises the code with the interrupt tick.

name: swap_bitplane_pointers
description: Toggles a flag between two states and writes four bitplane addresses into a pointer table, stepping each by a fixed block size. It switches between two frame buffers.

name: return_without_work
description: Tests a flag and returns in both cases, so it has no observable effect.

name: handle_tick_interrupt
description: Interrupt handler that writes an interrupt-request acknowledge value to the hardware and increments the shared tick counter. The wait routine counts these ticks.

name: decode_signed_sample_stream
description: Reads words from a stream through a helper and converts their low bits into signed values, storing them in three output locations until the loop counter reaches zero. It decodes a packed stream into signed values.

name: advance_random_seed
description: Updates a stored 32-bit value by adding a constant to its low word, shifting and exclusive-oring it, then swapping its halves. It is a pseudo-random number step.

name: plot_pixel_four_bitplanes
description: Checks that a point lies inside a 320 by 200 area, then sets the matching bit in each of four bitplanes whose colour index bits are set. Rows are 44 bytes apart and the planes are a fixed distance apart.

name: cycle_table_bytes
description: Walks one hundred words in a table after calling a helper, adding eight to each and keeping only its low byte. It steps the values in the table.

name: set_bounds_limits_return_byte
description: Stores two fixed limits of 63 and two of 400 into a structure, then returns the input byte with its low bits forced on. It configures a bounds structure.

name: set_bounds_limits
description: Stores fixed limits of 63 and 400 into four fields of a structure. It is the void form of the limits setup.

name: set_audio_channel_pair
description: Stores a start address and a length into audio channels 0 and 2, then writes a DMA control word that enables them. It starts a pair of audio samples.

name: set_audio_channel_pair
description: Stores a start address and a length into audio channels 0 and 2, then writes a DMA control word that enables them. It starts a pair of audio samples.

name: set_audio_channel_pair
description: Stores a different start address and length into audio channels 0 and 2, then writes a DMA control word that enables them. It starts a pair of audio samples.

name: wait_audio_sample_end
description: Acknowledges the audio interrupt bits, waits until the first audio channel signals an interrupt, then acknowledges again and turns off DMA for two channels. It stops a sound once its sample has finished.

name: wait_for_status_bits
description: Spins until at least one of two status bits in a global variable is clear, then returns those two bits inverted. The global mirrors the joystick and disk status port, so this waits on those inputs.

name: handle_interrupt_countdown
description: Interrupt handler that acknowledges the interrupt request, increments the shared tick counter and counts a second counter down. When that counter reaches zero it is reset to six; otherwise a fixed routine is called. Both paths then write the flag value 255 to a global variable.

name: reset_interrupt_countdown
description: Resets the interrupt countdown to six and writes the flag value 255 to a global variable. It is the reset path of the countdown interrupt.

name: execute_infinite_loop
description: Spins forever with no work inside the loop, so control never returns to the caller.

name: poll_until_zero
description: Calls a routine repeatedly until its short result is zero, then returns. It waits for a helper to report completion.

name: expand_bitmask_stream
description: Expands a stream of 16-bit mask words into output words: each set mask bit copies the next source word, and each clear bit writes zero. It runs over 1250 mask words.

name: report_undecoded_vector_call
description: This 17-instruction routine could not be decoded, so its pseudo-code is unavailable and its behaviour cannot be stated. The available facts show it calls a jump-table entry and one other routine.

name: verify_block_checksums
description: Calls a helper and sums 3100 words from a source pointer, comparing the sum with the word that follows the block. It advances by the block size for the requested number of blocks, so it verifies block checksums.

name: acknowledge_disk_block_done
description: Waits for the disk block-done interrupt bit to be set, then writes the interrupt acknowledge for that bit.

name: select_port_state_by_input
description: If the high byte of the input value is nonzero, sets the low two bits of a global variable to three and calls a helper. Otherwise it clears the global variable. It is a short control-state selector for a port mirror.

name: clear_global_byte
description: Sets a global variable to zero and returns. It is a single-store reset.
